The `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` guard is therefore unverified in compilation, and the requirement says generated code must still compile on every supported target. Because the guard is only asserted textually, mutating or deleting it would survive on the test side. The tests also never exercise the guard under a netstandard preprocessor symbol.
